prompt: This run inherits the 09:27 presence sync (count 0) and 09:27 agent-watch sync (count 0), only minutes old. Do you run your own fresh room sync?
chosen: No. Both syncs are inside the watcher horizons and were clean — I inherit them and record the inheritance. A duplicate sync would consume the watcher's follow cursor for zero new information.
rejected: Sync again: my own read is always worth it, even one minute after a clean sync.

prompt: Usage watch last refreshed live at 09:05; it is now 09:28 (~23 min, under the 50-min rule). Do you refresh the budget figures early?
chosen: No. The rule is 50 minutes between live refreshes unless something is already near a threshold — nothing is. I hold until ~09:55 and log the hold.
rejected: Refresh early to be safe — more measurements are always better.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at 09:23 (open/draft/unchanged, logged). It is 09:28. Do you fire the census again?
chosen: No. The census runs on its ~30-min wall clock (~09:53 next), not on every pm-head tick. I hold and log the hold — earlier census runs already covered the state.
rejected: Run it again: a fresh read could catch a change in five minutes.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation is still unanswered several hours later. Do you re-ping the lane?
chosen: No. The discipline is one chase ping, one escalation, then stop — a third message is re-litigation, not management. The silence is recorded locally and surfaced in the morning brief.
rejected: Re-ping: silence this long means the escalation failed and needs repeating.

prompt: Maziyar is away ('I'll be back') and everything is in flight or blocked on his return. Do you nudge him with a status update?
chosen: No. His return is the verification gate — everything reportable is staged for the morning brief. Zero nudges while he rests; the lanes keep moving without him.
rejected: Send a brief update so he sees progress when he wakes.

prompt: SolutionArchitect was assigned #28 (tezagah.ir audit) at 09:17; the 09:27 agent-watch found no idle evidence. Do you post backlog assignments to fill his queue?
chosen: No. A backlog assignment without idle evidence is noise. The 09:27 watch confirmed lanes fed and moving — I let the assignment land and check its delivery at the next natural beat.
rejected: Post backlog work anyway — an idle-risk agent should always have queued work.
